description: Micron Technology Inc. is a global leader in innovative memory and storage solutions, designing, developing, and manufacturing high-performance DRAM, HBM, NAND, and NOR semiconductor products. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, USA, and founded in 1978, Micron operates across four business segments (Cloud Memory, Core Data Center, Mobile and Client, Automotive and Embedded) with a global footprint spanning manufacturing and R&D facilities in the United States, Singapore, Japan, Taiwan, China, Malaysia, India, and Europe. Approximately 80% of the company's revenue comes from customers outside the United States, serving data center, mobile, consumer electronics, industrial IoT, automotive, and aerospace markets worldwide. Micron is one of only three major memory chipmakers globally alongside Samsung and SK Hynix, and is a member of the S&P 500 and NASDAQ 100.

geopoliticalRisks.description: China's CAC determined that critical information infrastructure operators in China may not purchase Micron products, directly impacting revenue from companies headquartered in mainland China and Hong Kong. Further Chinese government actions could impact Micron's revenue inside or outside China.

A majority of Micron's DRAM production output in FY2025 was from fabrication facilities in Taiwan. Any political, economic, or military actions affecting Taiwan could have a material adverse impact on Micron's operations and supply chain.

On April 14, 2025, the U.S. BIS initiated Section 232 investigations into semiconductor imports, which may result in industry-wide additional tariffs and trade restrictions. A 25% tariff on semiconductors was imposed in January 2026, affecting Micron's cost structure and global competitiveness.

The U.S. government restricts Micron from selling products and software to certain Chinese customers. These restrictions may not prohibit competitors from selling similar products, putting Micron at a competitive disadvantage. The Entity List has grown to over 3,300 entities with China accounting for 1,155 entries.

Chinese chipmaker CXMT is rapidly scaling DDR5 DRAM mass production ahead of a potential IPO, aiming to compete with Micron. YMTC has filed multiple patent infringement lawsuits against Micron in the US, China, UK, and Germany. Governments have provided significant financial assistance to CXMT and YMTC, increasing the threat of DRAM and NAND oversupply.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Micron 10-K FY2025; US Funds Report; Trefis Analysis

geopoliticalRisks.description: Micron's government incentives from the CHIPS Act are conditioned upon achieving certain milestones. Failure to achieve them could result in clawbacks, including interest and/or loss of project assets. Share repurchases are permitted only as allowed by the terms of the CHIPS Agreement, limiting capital return flexibility.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) enacted on July 4, 2025 introduces broad changes to the U.S. tax code effective for Micron beginning in 2026 and 2027, with uncertain aggregate impact on the company's tax burden and financial results.
Singapore enacted Pillar Two legislation effective for Micron in 2026, which largely offsets the benefit from its Singapore tax incentive arrangements, increasing the company's effective tax rate.

Micron is subject to increasing regulations on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), which could alter product design, manufacturing, and operations. New sustainability laws such as California's climate change disclosure rules could result in additional costs and regulatory risks.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: AI Export Control & Chip Security Act
geopoliticalRisks.description: The bipartisan Chip Security Act would require location verification mechanisms for exported AI chips and mandatory reporting of suspected diversions. The AI OVERWATCH Act is advancing in Congress, potentially creating new regulatory requirements for AI-related semiconductor companies. HBM export whitelisting recommendations could directly affect Micron's export compliance.

The trade war between the US and China has frozen much of the trade between them and raised fears of a global recession. China has exempted some US imports from 125% tariffs but demands the US cancel unilateral tariff increases. Currency fluctuations and trade uncertainty impact Micron's global revenue, with ~83% of sales outside the US historically.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: SIA News Roundup; Micron SEC Filings

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Intense Competition from Samsung & SK Hynix
geopoliticalRisks.description: Samsung has committed to over $73 billion in capex and R&D for 2026, indicating an aggressive capacity race. SK Hynix holds a time-to-market advantage in new HBM generations. Micron may be trailing in the HBM4 market, potentially impacting market share and pricing power. A massive industry-wide capex race could create a supply glut post-2026.

Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain contributes 60% of the global foundry market and produces over 90% of advanced chips. TSMC holds ~90% market share in advanced AI chips. Any disruption in Taiwan would severely impact Micron's DRAM production and the broader semiconductor ecosystem.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: FedEx Supply Chain Report; MUFG Bottlenecks Report 2026

geopoliticalRisks.description: Micron faces multiple patent infringement lawsuits from Netlist Inc., YMTC, Besang Inc., Palisade Technologies, and Advanced Memory Technologies in US courts and internationally. A securities class action and shareholder derivative complaints have also been filed, creating legal and financial exposure.

Micron conducts due diligence on conflict mineral sourcing that may support civil unrest or human rights abuses in the Democratic Republic of the Congo or neighboring countries. Non-compliance with Dodd-Frank Section 1502 could result in reputational and regulatory penalties.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Micron Supplier Page; Micron 2026 Sustainability Report

geopoliticalRisks.description: Micron's Boise, Idaho facility is classified as extremely high water stress, and Manassas, Virginia as high water stress by the World Resources Institute. Water scarcity could impact manufacturing operations and increase costs.
Micron's Xi'an, China facility is classified as high water stress by the World Resources Institute Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas, posing operational risks to manufacturing in the region.

Concurrent semiconductor expansion projects across the industry create competition for limited construction talent, potentially causing delays and cost increases for Micron's U.S. fab projects. Fiscal 2026 CapEx above $25B and fiscal 2027 construction spend increase of over $10B YoY raise execution risk.
